prompt: What does the lesson say to write before opening the BI tool?

choices.text: A list of every chart that might be relevant
choices.why: That is how pages nobody opens get built.
Right. A named person, a known schedule, a short list.

choices.text: The colour palette for the page
The SQL for the detail table at the bottom of the page

prompt: Match each kind of dashboard to its reader's rhythm.
Lantern's owner also wants to follow the Black Friday cohort. Why does the lesson keep it off the Monday page?

choices.text: Cohorts cannot be drawn in Metabase

choices.why: Right. It gets a page of its own.

choices.text: Because the page already has more than ten charts, which is the most Metabase allows
choices.why: There is no such limit, and the page has few.

prompt: Put the bands of a tactical dashboard in order, from the top of the page.
trap: Trend before headline is the usual slip: the eye lands at the top left, where the answer belongs.

prompt: Why does Lantern's page carry a text card saying when the data ends?

choices.text: So nobody reads June's partial bar as a collapse
choices.why: Right. A caveat on the page beats one in somebody's head.

choices.text: Metabase requires one on every dashboard
Because the database cannot store dates beyond 17 June
choices.why: That is when the extract ended.

prompt: Why does the page have three tiles and not eight?

choices.text: Metabase limits the number of tiles
Eight would not fit on a phone screen in portrait mode

choices.why: Right. A tile that answers none of them is a candidate for removal.

choices.text: Three is a rule of design
choices.why: The number follows the questions, not a rule.

prompt: R$ 140,097.06 of net revenue in May 2026. What does the lesson say the number alone tells the reader?

choices.text: That May was a good month
Nothing about whether it is good
choices.why: Right. A number beside the right comparison is information; alone it is not.
The target is a separate comparison.
It rose, but the number alone does not say so.

prompt: By what percentage did May 2026's net revenue exceed April's? One decimal place.
Why does the year-on-year comparison stay off Lantern's tile?

choices.why: It can: more than six times.

choices.text: It answers no question on the list, and measures the shop's birth
choices.why: Right. Lesson 4 made the same point.

choices.text: It would make the page too slow
Year-on-year figures are banned by the owner

prompt: What does "a change needs its base" mean on a tile?

choices.text: Show the change in points, never in percent
Use the first month of data as the base for every comparison on the page
Show the number large and the change beside it
choices.why: Right. +16.9% alone hides whether it came from 100 or 100,000.

prompt: What does `lag(net_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)` return on each row?

choices.why: Right. The row before, in the order given.
`lag` moves one row unless told otherwise.

choices.text: The running total up to that month, as a year-to-date figure would show

prompt: What change against May does the naive month-on-month query report for June 2026? One decimal place.
Monday 15 June has 43 orders and Sunday 14 June has 10. Which comparison does the lesson recommend for the Monday?

choices.text: With the Sunday before, since it is the previous day

choices.why: Right. 43 against 38: the same weekday a week earlier.
A different weekday, and a baby shop.

prompt: June 1–17 brought R$ 75,811.94 and May 1–17 brought R$ 82,271.16. What is June's change on the same days? One decimal place.
hint: June divided by May, minus one.

prompt: Where should "data until" on a dashboard come from?

choices.why: On the day a load fails, today is wrong.
Right. Only the data knows when it ends.

choices.text: The schedule of the extract job as configured by the platform team
choices.why: A schedule says when it should run, not whether it did.

prompt: Which habits does the lesson give for a partial period? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Compare it with the same part of the previous period
Mark the partial bar when it must be shown
Multiply it by 30/17 and show it as a complete month

prompt: Where does Lantern's target come from?

choices.text: It is computed from last year's revenue

choices.why: Right. A target is a decision, stored where a query can read it.

choices.text: The average of the six months

prompt: June's target is R$ 145,000. Pro-rated to 17 of 30 days, what is it, in reais? Nearest real.
Why must a red or green status carry a word or a number beside it?

choices.text: Words are faster to read than colours for everybody
Many readers cannot tell red from green
choices.why: Right. About one man in twelve has some colour vision deficiency.

prompt: Two managers read the same amber tile differently. What does the lesson say was missing?

choices.text: The threshold, written down with its owner
choices.why: Right. Who decided 95% is amber is a definition like any other.
Colour does not carry meaning on its own.
Size does not define a threshold.

prompt: The North's revenue rose 169% from January to February 2026. What should a dashboard show beside that figure?

choices.why: A comparison of a different kind.
Right. A rate on a handful of events is noise wearing the clothes of a finding.

prompt: May 2026: the Southeast brought R$ 106,548.18 of R$ 140,097.06. What share is that? Nearest whole percent.
How does the lesson say to sort a breakdown by region?

choices.why: The eye then meets the North before the Southeast.
Right. Their order of importance to the business.

choices.text: By the change on last month, largest first
choices.why: That promotes the noisiest small regions.

prompt: Why does the lesson say the default value of a filter is the dashboard for most people?

choices.text: Most readers never touch a filter
choices.why: Right. Whatever the default shows is what they read.

choices.text: Because every filter resets to the author's last choice

prompt: A region filter is connected to the trend and not to the tiles. What does a reader set to South see?

choices.text: Tiles about everybody, a trend about the South
choices.why: Right. With nothing on the page to say so.

choices.text: A blank page until every card is connected

prompt: How does the lesson suggest catching a filter that silently drops rows?

choices.why: The check is on the page.

choices.text: Look for warnings in Metabase's log
Compare a total with the filter on "all" against no filter
choices.why: Right. A difference means rows fell out through the filter.

prompt: Put the steps of building the Monday page in Metabase in order.
items: save each question with a description
Add questions, in the four bands
add the text card with the caveats
add a date filter and connect it card by card

prompt: For the month-to-date comparison tile, why does the lesson suggest a SQL question rather than the editor?

choices.why: Right. Same days of the previous month need the explicit query.

choices.text: The editor cannot read the semantic schema at all, only raw tables
choices.why: It reads the layer; lesson 3 used it.

prompt: On 17 June the page says "data until 12 June". What does it tell the reader?

choices.why: It is the data that stopped.
Right. Before acting on any number.

choices.text: That the dashboard is cached for a week by design

choices.why: It is the most important line on the page that day.

prompt: Put the remedies for a slow dashboard in the order the lesson says to try them.
trap: Pre-aggregating first is the usual slip: it costs the most, and the cheaper two often suffice.

prompt: A pre-aggregated table is rebuilt at 3 a.m. What must the page then say?

choices.why: They are exact, as of a time.

choices.text: That its numbers are as of 3 a.m.
choices.why: Right. Never trade correctness for speed silently.

choices.text: That readers should refresh the browser every hour to get the latest numbers
choices.why: Refreshing the browser does not rebuild the table.

prompt: Match each review check to the question it asks.

pairs.right: is it complete, or compared with the same part of the last?
is it a rate on a handful of events?
does the page say when its data ends?
does a colour carry meaning alone?

prompt: Which two checks does the lesson say find the most?

choices.text: Filters and definitions, since they change most often between releases of the tool

prompt: What should every dashboard carry, according to the lesson's lifecycle section?

choices.why: Right. The person who answers when a number looks wrong.

choices.text: A public link so anybody can find it

prompt: A page has been opened only by its author for three months. What does the lesson suggest?

choices.text: Send it to everybody by e-mail
choices.why: Pushing it does not make it useful.

choices.text: Add more charts to attract readers
Delete its questions immediately, even those used on other pages, to save space in the collection
Retire it, and say where readers should look

prompt: On 10 June a tile shows June at 31% of its monthly target in red. What is wrong, and what is right?

choices.text: Nothing is wrong; June is behind
choices.why: A third of the month cannot be judged against the whole.

choices.text: A partial month was judged against a whole target; pro-rate or wait
choices.why: Right. And colour nothing until like is compared with like.
The threshold is not the problem.

prompt: A page opens filtered to the office segment because its author last looked at offices. What has the page become?

choices.text: A page that shows everybody its author's question
choices.why: Right. The default for every filter other than the date is "all".
Nobody is restricted; they just do not see the filter.
